blocks.text: I can use -er verbs in the simple present tense, including two-verb structures, to say what I do and like doing.
You will also learn to recognise and pronounce [oi].
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: the dictionary form of the verb giving its general meaning
phrase with two verbs, where the second verb is an infinitive

blocks.text: [oi] is pronounced as in ‘voir’. Read these words and say them aloud.
Avoir means to have, having. Au revoir means goodbye. Trois is 3.

items.q: Which word does NOT have the [oi] sound?

blocks.text: Change the infinitive to the singular form that matches the pronoun. For regular -er verbs the endings are je → -e, tu → -es and il/elle → -e.

items: Je trouve une solution. = I find a solution.
Tu trouves une solution. = You find a solution.
Elle trouve une solution. = She finds a solution.

blocks.text: The infinitive is trouver, which means to find, finding.

items.q: Je ____ (passer) un moment à la maison.

items: J’aime le professeur. = I like the teacher.
J’aime écouter le professeur. = I like listening to the teacher. (or: I like to listen to the teacher.)

blocks.text: In a two-verb structure, the second verb is an {infinitive} verb.
Use the correct ending on the first verb (je → aime). The second verb stays in its long form: écouter.
In English we can translate the infinitive as ‘to’ + verb or as ‘-ing’.

items: Il aime trouver la réponse. = He likes to find the answer.
Il aime trouver la réponse. = He likes finding the answer.

blocks.label: Which one do we usually say?
blocks.text: Both are right, but after ‘like’ it is more common to use -ing: He likes finding the answer.

blocks.why: If a sentence has two verbs, the second verb needs to be in the long form, the infinitive.

blocks.q: How do you say ‘He likes staying at home’?
options: Il aime reste à la maison.
Il aimes rester à la maison.
Il aime rester à la maison.
blocks.why: Il aime uses the -e ending, and the second verb stays as the infinitive: rester.

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: A French infinitive isn’t only translated with ‘to’. It can be ‘to’ + verb or ‘-ing’, like ‘to do’ or ‘doing’.

items: If a sentence has one present tense verb, the verb ending matches the pronoun. With -er verbs the endings are: je → -e, tu → -es and il/elle → -e.
In a two-verb structure, the second verb needs to be in the infinitive, the long form.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: What people like doing: 2-verb phrases with ‘aimer’
worksheet.instructions: Translate the sentences into French, or fill in the gaps. Remember the endings je → -e, tu → -es, il/elle → -e, and keep the second verb in the infinitive.

questions.prompt: Translate into French: ‘I spend a week in France.’
questions.answer: Je passe une semaine en France.
accepted: Je passe une semaine en France
je passe une semaine en France
questions.explanation: Je takes passe, and a week in France is une semaine en France.

questions.prompt: Translate into French: ‘Do you like the cooking at school?’
questions.answer: Tu aimes la cuisine à l’école ?
accepted: Tu aimes la cuisine à l'école ?
Tu aimes la cuisine à l’école
Tu aimes la cuisine à l'école
Tu aimes la cuisine à l’école?
Tu aimes la cuisine à l'école?
questions.explanation: Tu takes aimes, and the cooking at school is la cuisine à l’école.

questions.prompt: Translate into French: ‘He stays a week with a friend (m).’
questions.answer: Il reste une semaine avec un ami.
accepted: Il reste une semaine avec un ami
il reste une semaine avec un ami
questions.explanation: Il takes reste, and with a (male) friend is avec un ami.

questions.prompt: Translate into French: ‘I tick the homework in class.’
questions.answer: Je coche les devoirs en classe.
accepted: Je coche les devoirs en classe
je coche les devoirs en classe
questions.explanation: Je takes coche, homework is les devoirs, and in class is en classe.

questions.prompt: Translate into French: ‘She likes shopping in France.’ (food shopping)
questions.answer: Elle aime les courses en France.
accepted: Elle aime faire les courses en France
Elle aime faire les courses en France.
Elle aime les courses en France
elle aime les courses en France
questions.explanation: Elle takes aime, and shopping is les courses.

questions.prompt: Translate into French: ‘You find the answer with a friend (f).’
questions.answer: Tu trouves la réponse avec une amie.
accepted: Tu trouves la réponse avec une amie
tu trouves la réponse avec une amie
questions.explanation: Tu takes trouves, and with a (female) friend is avec une amie.

questions.prompt: Translate into French: ‘She finds the sentence in class.’
questions.answer: Elle trouve la phrase en classe.
accepted: Elle trouve la phrase en classe
elle trouve la phrase en classe
questions.explanation: Elle takes trouve, the sentence is la phrase, and in class is en classe.

questions.prompt: Translate into French: ‘Do you wear a uniform at school?’
questions.answer: Tu portes un uniforme à l’école ?
accepted: Tu portes un uniforme à l'école ?
Tu portes un uniforme à l’école
Tu portes un uniforme à l'école
Tu portes un uniforme à l’école?
Tu portes un uniforme à l'école?
questions.explanation: Tu takes portes, and at school is à l’école.

questions.prompt: Translate into English: Elle aime écouter la chanteuse.
questions.answer: She likes listening to the singer.
accepted: She likes listening to the singer
She likes to listen to the singer
she likes listening to the singer
She likes to listen to the singer.
questions.explanation: Aime is the elle form of aimer, and the second verb écouter is an infinitive: listening or to listen.

questions.prompt: Translate into English: Tu aimes avoir un chien ?
questions.answer: Do you like having a dog?
accepted: Do you like having a dog
Do you like to have a dog?
Do you like to have a dog
do you like having a dog?
questions.explanation: Tu aimes is ‘you like’, and the infinitive avoir means having or to have.

questions.prompt: Fill in the gap with the correct verb form: J’aime ____ les solutions. (to find)
accepted: Trouver
questions.explanation: The second verb in a two-verb structure stays in the infinitive: trouver.
